newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Jan 8.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
BIG LET DOWN AS BRANSON CALLS IT OFF
Richard Branson has been forced by technical problems to abandon his second attempt to go around the world in a balloon, less than a day into the journey.
CABLE TV DEAL CUTS SCHOOL INTERNET COSTS

The cable television industry is promoting new fixed-priced packages which will remove the problem of running up huge telephone bills for schools wanting to connect to the Internet, in a direct challenge to BT. Telecoms regulator Don Cruickshank has welcomed the deal, which means schools will pay no more than one stg per year.

Robert Fleming, the investment bank, is to issue the first London-listed Eurobond convertible into the shares of a central European company. Fleming plans to launch the deal, which is aimed at raising 30m pounds stg for Stalexport, an integrated steel company based in Katowice, south western Poland, at the end of March, and expects there to be significant British and European interest.
WATER GROUPS IN BID TO TAP INTO MANILA
Anglian Water and United Utilities have submitted separate bids for a 25-year contract to run Manila's water and sewage system.
PEPTECH OF AUSTRALIA TARGETS A UK LISTING

Peptech, the Australian pharmaceuticals company which develops and markets health and fertility products for humans and the veterinary market, is planning to list in London in February. Such a move will test the appetite of British investors for big-tech stocks.
